draft.title: Commission and piecework
card: Pay worked out as a percentage of the value of what a person sells. Commission = rate × sales.
Pay worked out as a fixed amount for each item made or task done. Piecework pay = rate per item × number of items.
Sam sells $12 000 of furniture at 5% commission. Commission = 0.05 × 12 000 = $600. Ana is paid $4 for each scarf she sews and sews 30. Pay = 4 × 30 = $120.
Some workers get a base wage or salary and commission on top. Add the two to find total pay.
draft.remember: Commission pays a percentage of sales. Piecework pays a set amount per item or task.

a.q: Leila earns 4% commission on her sales. She sells $15 000 of solar panels in a month. How much commission does she earn?
a.why: Commission = 4% × 15 000 = 0.04 × 15 000 = $600. Dividing 15 000 by 4 gives $3750, which treats 4% as 1/4 and is wrong.
a.clue: Change 4% to a decimal, then multiply by the sales.

b.q: Tom is paid a base wage of $500 a week plus 3% commission on his sales. In one week he sells $8000 of goods. What is his total pay for the week?
b.why: Commission = 0.03 × 8000 = $240. Total pay = base wage + commission = 500 + 240 = $740. Giving $240 leaves out the base wage.
b.clue: Work out the commission first, then add the base wage.
